description:
MT-2c (Sprint 51, F129): the Review No Rule Items screen's COVERED-ITEM SWEEP -- the Sprint 50 fix that runs `_sweepCoveredItems` on EVERY load of the screen rather than only after a bulk action. READ-ONLY and idempotent: toggles account-filter chips and selects/deselects rows (transient UI state only). It creates no rules, adds no safe senders, and marks nothing processed, so it is inherently net-zero on the dev DB. SELECTORS AND INTERACTION MODEL VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-28 against dev build 0.5.8; REWORKED 2026-08-15 (Sprint 59): F135 (Sprint 52) made this screen the app default, so the home-screen entry-point steps were structurally stale (the screen has no self-referential icon; it IS home), the reload tooltip was renamed from 'Refresh' to 'Re-check the last scan (does not fetch new mail)' in Sprint 52, the screen name lost its nested quotes per F155, and the two baseline sender rows were refreshed to senders present in the 2026-08-15 dev DB; STATUS 2026-08-16 after anonymization: the anonymized selectors RESOLVE AND CLICK correctly (verified live -- step 6 passed against the real app); the run then failed at step 7 with 'Cannot access a disposed object', a harness/app-teardown fault unrelated to the selectors. The full 3/3 sweep evidence for Sprint 60 was captured BEFORE this change (see SPRINT_60_PLAN.md). Re-verify this script at the next sweep. ANONYMIZED 2026-08-16 per the PR #335 Copilot review and the Sprint 59 precedent (commit 891411b): row selectors match the correspondent's DOMAIN only, never the local part, so no real person's address is committed to a public repo. The two baselines must remain DISTINCT domains (the assertion rests on both surviving the sweep). Refreshed again 2026-08-16 (Sprint 60 close-out sweep) after Harold's MV rule/safe-sender additions addressed the previous baseline rows -- exactly the data-precondition case this header documents. Post-F135 a true cold RE-MOUNT of the screen is no longer reachable from the UI (the root route stays alive under pushed routes), so the old 're-entry' case now proves a navigation round-trip instead; the fresh-mount sweep behaviour is deterministically covered by the widget test (`no_rule_review_screen_test`).

WHAT THIS ASSERTS, AND WHY IT NEEDS NO NEW RULE. The sweep's contract is: on every load, drop items now covered by a rule or safe sender, and leave everything else alone. The dev DB holds thousands of rules and hundreds of safe senders, so EVERY load of this screen runs the sweep against that full rule set -- the code path is exercised without writing anything. The failure mode worth guarding is OVER-COLLECTION: a sweep that wrongly drops uncovered items, which is exactly the MT-2b/MT-2c bug shape Harold reported in Sprint 50 (items vanishing from the list). This script therefore asserts STABILITY across repeated loads: named rows that are present on the first load must still be present after a reload and after a navigation round-trip. If the sweep over-collects, those selectors resolve 0 elements and the run FAILS.

WHY NOT CREATE A RULE FIRST (the obvious design, deliberately rejected 2026-07-28): a create-then-delete variant was written and abandoned after the create path proved hostile to automation on this build -- the Rule Type RadioButton does NOT select via ww_click on either the RadioButton or its parent Group (the form silently stays in its default Entire-Domain mode), the 'Save Rule' button sits off-screen unless the window is maximized (ww_invoke reports success on it WITHOUT pressing it; ww_click correctly errors 'element_offscreen'), and synthetic domains are rejected by input validation so no confirm dialog ever appears. Those are the same obstacles that keep the two F56 create/delete scripts EXCLUDED from the default sweep. Blocking a REAL listed sender was rejected separately: those rows are Harold's live scanned mail, and an item's covered state is not cleanly reversible from the UI, so the script could not honour the Sprint 37 restore-what-you-modify policy. Verifying the sweep's create-side behaviour deterministically belongs in the widget test (`no_rule_review_screen_test`), which already models a pre-existing covering rule and asserts all matching items are removed on the FIRST load with no user action.

HARNESS FACTS (all established by failing runs on 2026-07-28, not assumed):
(1) USE ww_invoke, NOT ww_click, for Buttons -- ww_click reported success WITHOUT activating controls on a cold-launched app. EXCEPTIONS, which must use ww_click with useInvokePattern:false because they do not support InvokePattern: TabBar tabs and static Text nodes ('Element does not support InvokePattern. ControlType: Text') and CheckBoxes, which expose TogglePattern ('...ControlType: CheckBox').
(2) A step reporting success proves DISPATCH, not effect. `ww_assert*` is not replayable by the runner, so every navigation is followed by a step that can only resolve if the app really advanced.
(3) Flutter builds its UIA semantics tree LAZILY in response to a query, not on a timer -- a 10-second wait does NOT help. The leading ww_window_state is the priming query.
(4) ww_invoke does NOT verify visibility: it will report success on an off-screen element without pressing it. ww_click errors 'element_offscreen' instead. Maximize first.

PRECONDITION -- THIS SCRIPT REQUIRES AT LEAST 2 UNADDRESSED NO-RULE ROWS. Baseline rows are data-dependent (Harold's live scanned mail): if the list is EMPTY (e.g., right after a Manual Validation session that addressed everything, as on 2026-08-15), the row-checkbox steps resolve 0 elements and the script fails at step 6 -- that is a DATA-PRECONDITION failure, not a regression (the chip/navigation steps still pass). Refresh the two sender names from a live ww_dump_tree whenever the pool changes. Future work: a deterministic seeding preamble (insert/remove synthetic unmatched_emails rows around the run) would remove the live-data dependence entirely.

testCases.title: Post-F135 home screen: the sweep produces a coherent list with named rows

steps._comment: PRIMING QUERY (fact 3) -- also guarantees a maximized window so nothing is off-screen (fact 4).

Post-F135 the app OPENS on this screen when accounts exist; the 'All Accounts' chip exists only here, so it resolving is the reachability proof. Reaching this point means _loadItems -- and therefore _sweepCoveredItems -- has already run once against the full rule/safe-sender set. The account chips carry the POST-sweep counts in their accessible names; prefix-matched because counts are data-dependent.
BASELINE ROW A. Each row exposes a 'Select <sender>' checkbox thanks to the Sprint 51 F129 semantics work. CheckBox needs ww_click (TogglePattern, not InvokePattern -- fact 1).
PROOF OF EFFECT: 'Clear' is rendered only once a row is genuinely selected, so it proves the checkbox actually toggled rather than the click merely being dispatched. It is also the state restore.
BASELINE ROW B -- a second, different sender, so the assertion is not resting on a single row.

testCases.title: MT-2c CORE: reload re-runs the sweep in place -- it must be idempotent, not progressively eat the list

steps._comment: The reload button re-enters _loadItems, so the sweep runs a SECOND time over the same data. The Sprint 50 MT-2b/MT-2c bug shape was items disappearing across reloads; a correct sweep is idempotent. Tooltip renamed from 'Refresh' in Sprint 52.
steps.selector: type=Button[name='Re-check the last scan (does not fetch new mail)']

steps._comment: THE ASSERTION: both baseline rows must SURVIVE the second sweep. Neither sender is covered by any existing rule (they are in the No-Rule list precisely because nothing covers them), so a correct sweep leaves both alone. If the sweep over-collected, these resolve 0 elements and the run FAILS.
A THIRD sweep, to catch a slow leak that a single reload would miss.
steps.selector: type=Button[name='Re-check the last scan (does not fetch new mail)']

steps._comment: The chips must still report coherent post-sweep counts after three sweeps.

testCases.title: Navigation round-trip: leave via Scan History, return, rows still present

steps._comment: Leave the screen and come back. Post-F135 the root route stays ALIVE under pushed routes, so this is a round-trip check (screen intact after navigation), NOT a cold re-mount -- that fresh-mount sweep case is deterministically covered by the widget test instead.
THE ASSERTION, after the round-trip: both rows must still be present, and selection state must still work.
Teardown proof: still on the home screen, chips intact, selection cleared, nothing written.
